text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock jumped 4.5% today, capping an 18% surge over the past week, driven by a sharp spike in crude oil prices triggered by Iranian tanker attacks and geopolitical tensions in the Gulf. The global oil price has climbed to $125 per barrel—well above the U.S. price of $96—while U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% capacity with inventory levels that support sustained demand. For a major refiner like Marathon, higher crude prices combined with full refinery utilization and tight product supplies create the conditions for improved margins on both gasoline and diesel sales.

The broader backdrop amplifies these gains: political pressure over fuel costs, hurricane threats to Gulf production, and discussions of potential U.S. military action in Iran all point to an extended period of elevated energy prices and geopolitical risk premium. That uncertainty and supply tightness, combined with a refiner already operating near capacity, typically benefits margin-heavy integrated oil and fuel producers.
